title: Compound nouns: meaning, order and measurement
summary: Build noun compounds in which an earlier noun describes the main noun, interpret longer chains and -ing forms, and distinguish an object intended for something from a container holding it. Use singular modifiers and hyphenated measurements before nouns.
learningObjectives: Form common noun + noun compounds and identify which final noun names the main person, object or place.
Interpret longer noun chains and established compounds containing -ing.
Distinguish a purpose-based compound, such as a tea cup, from an of-phrase describing its contents.
Use singular noun modifiers and singular, hyphenated measurement expressions such as a six-day project.

explanation.heading: The head noun and the describing noun
explanation.body: In a noun compound, the last noun is normally the head: it names the person, thing or place. Earlier nouns give a type, purpose, material, subject or connection. A garden chair is a chair for a garden, and a customer survey is a survey involving customers. Many compounds can be understood from the relationship between the words, but the intended relationship also depends on context.
explanation.example: The café installed a new water filter beside the sink.

explanation.heading: Longer chains and -ing modifiers
explanation.body: Compounds may contain three or more nouns, especially in work and service contexts. Read them from the last noun backwards: a visitor parking permit is a permit for visitor parking. Some fixed modifiers end in -ing, as in a training room, a parking space or a cooking lesson. The -ing form here helps name the type or purpose of the head noun.
explanation.example: The supervisor signed the factory safety inspection report.

explanation.heading: Spelling compounds
explanation.body: English uses solid compounds, open compounds and sometimes hyphenated compounds. For example, notebook is one word, bus stop is two, and a well-known type may use a hyphen. There is no reliable rule that predicts every compound spelling. Check a dictionary for established words, and avoid joining two nouns just because they form one idea.
explanation.example: Our visitor left a notebook on the bus stop bench.

explanation.heading: Purpose versus actual contents
explanation.body: A compound can describe what an item is intended for, even if it is empty. A tea cup is the kind of cup used for tea; a cup of tea tells us that the cup contains tea. Likewise, a shopping basket may be empty, while a basket of groceries contains purchased food or other items. When you need to state actual contents, an of-phrase is often clearer.
explanation.example: The empty tea cup stood next to a full cup of hot chocolate.

explanation.heading: Singular modifiers and measured descriptions
explanation.body: An attributive noun before a second noun is usually singular even when the meaning involves several items: a ticket machine sells tickets, and a book shelf can hold many books. The same pattern appears in measurements used before a noun, often with a hyphen: a six-day conference, a twenty-minute walk. After the noun, use an ordinary plural measure: the conference lasts six days. Some established compounds are exceptions to the singular-modifier tendency.
explanation.example: Our team finished a five-day workshop that required five days of attendance.

comparisons.title: An object type versus what is inside it

left.label: Purpose or type
left.note: Tea cup names the kind of cup, without saying it contains tea.

right.label: Actual contents
right.example: There is a cup of tea on the table.
right.note: A cup of tea refers to a quantity of tea in a cup.

comparisons.title: Measurement before a noun versus after a verb

left.label: Before a noun
left.note: Hour stays singular in the hyphenated modifier six-hour.

right.label: Following a verb
right.note: The unit hours is plural when giving the duration directly.

examples.sentence: The tourist information desk is beside the main entrance.
examples.note: Desk is the head noun; tourist information describes its purpose.

examples.sentence: She left the lunch box empty on the kitchen counter.
examples.note: A lunch box is intended to hold lunch even when empty.

examples.sentence: The reception team reviewed the staff training schedule.
examples.note: Schedule is the head noun of a three-noun chain.

examples.sentence: A swimming lesson is scheduled for Thursday.
examples.note: Swimming functions as an -ing modifier that describes the lesson.

examples.sentence: It was a nine-hour bus journey, although the journey felt shorter.
examples.note: Nine-hour is a singular hyphenated modifier before journey.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The museum has installed a new tickets machine.
commonMistakes.correct: The museum has installed a new ticket machine.
commonMistakes.why: Use the normally singular modifier ticket before machine.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We booked a four days workshop for the volunteers.
commonMistakes.correct: We booked a four-day workshop for the volunteers.
commonMistakes.why: A compound duration before a noun uses a singular unit with a hyphen.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She works for a company travel in the city centre.
commonMistakes.correct: She works for a travel company in the city centre.
commonMistakes.why: The describing noun travel comes before the head noun company.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The repair took three-hour to complete.
commonMistakes.correct: The repair took three hours to complete.
commonMistakes.why: After a verb, a measured duration uses the plural noun hours rather than a hyphenated modifier.

studyTips: Read a chain backwards from its final head noun: safety inspection report is a report about a safety inspection.
Ask whether the first noun expresses an intended purpose or whether an of-phrase is needed for actual contents.
Contrast a ten-minute break with the break lasts ten minutes to practise singular modifiers and plural amounts.

exercises.prompt: The container is empty, but it was made for carrying sandwiches. It is a ___.
exercises.feedback: A sandwich box names the intended type of container, even when it is empty.

exercises.prompt: A report describing staff training is a ___.
exercises.feedback: The head noun is report; staff training identifies its subject.

exercises.prompt: We registered for a ___ conference that runs from Monday to Thursday.
exercises.feedback: Before the noun conference, use the singular, hyphenated duration four-day.

exercises.prompt: The new ___ is large enough for two cars, but only one space is currently occupied.
exercises.feedback: Car parking area identifies a place used for parking cars; car is the usual singular noun modifier.

exercises.prompt: The train company installed a new ___ near the entrance. (Combine ticket + machine, in that order.)
acceptedAnswers: ticket machine
exercises.feedback: Ticket is the singular modifier of machine.

exercises.prompt: The manager asked us to review the ___ before Friday. (Combine safety + inspection + report in that order.)
acceptedAnswers: safety inspection report
exercises.feedback: Report is the final head noun, modified by safety inspection.

exercises.prompt: It is a ___ training programme for new employees. (Change six weeks into one hyphenated modifier.)
acceptedAnswers: six-week
exercises.feedback: Use a singular measurement unit and a hyphen before another noun.

exercises.prompt: I left my tea in a ___ beside the kettle. (Combine tea + cup as an object type; do not use an of-phrase.)
acceptedAnswers: tea cup
exercises.feedback: Tea cup names the type of cup, while a cup of tea would describe its contents.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The airport has installed two new passports scanners.
acceptedAnswers: The airport has installed two new passport scanners.
exercises.feedback: Passport is the normally singular noun modifier of scanners.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Maya joined a six weeks internship in June.
acceptedAnswers: Maya joined a six-week internship in June.
exercises.feedback: A measurement modifier before internship uses six-week, not six weeks.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Our guests waited at the reception hotel desk.
acceptedAnswers: Our guests waited at the hotel reception desk.
exercises.feedback: The noun chain is ordered hotel reception desk: desk is the head noun.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The guided tour lasts two-hour.
acceptedAnswers: The guided tour lasts two hours.
exercises.feedback: A duration after lasts uses plural hours, without a hyphen.

speakingExercises.prompt: Name this kind of item in a complete sentence: a bag designed for carrying laptops, even when empty. Begin with “This is” and use “laptop bag”.
acceptedAnswers: This is a laptop bag.
speakingExercises.feedback: Laptop specifies the bag’s purpose; it does not say there is a laptop inside.

speakingExercises.prompt: The bottle is empty but designed to carry water. Say one sentence using: the water bottle / be / empty. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: The water bottle is empty.
speakingExercises.feedback: Water bottle names the intended use; the bottle can still be empty.

speakingExercises.prompt: A customer asks what you purchased this morning. Use the exact words “train ticket” in a full sentence beginning “I bought” and ending “this morning”.
acceptedAnswers: I bought a train ticket this morning.
speakingExercises.feedback: Train modifies the head noun ticket.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the duration modifier and say the complete sentence: “We have a two hours meeting today.”
acceptedAnswers: We have a two-hour meeting today.
speakingExercises.feedback: Two-hour is the correct modifier before meeting.

speakingExercises.prompt: State this need in one sentence: we; need; a garden chair; for the patio. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: We need a garden chair for the patio.
speakingExercises.feedback: Garden is a noun modifier describing the type of chair.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give a precise location using this three-noun phrase: the hotel reception desk. Say “The keys are at” followed by that phrase.
acceptedAnswers: The keys are at the hotel reception desk.
speakingExercises.feedback: The final word desk is the head noun of the compound.

speakingExercises.prompt: Produce exactly two sentences with these facts: the internship lasts six weeks; it is a six-week internship. Use the exact wording given, and begin the second sentence with “It”.
acceptedAnswers: The internship lasts six weeks. It is a six-week internship.
The internship lasts six weeks. It’s a six-week internship.
speakingExercises.feedback: Six weeks is a duration after lasts; six-week is a singular modifier before internship.

speakingExercises.prompt: An empty cup is intended for coffee. Say one complete sentence beginning “The coffee cup” and ending “empty”.
acceptedAnswers: The coffee cup is empty.
speakingExercises.feedback: Coffee cup names its usual purpose, not its current contents.

listeningExercises.audioText: The technician ordered a new coffee machine, but the delivery included no coffee at all.
listeningExercises.prompt: What was delivered without its usual contents?
listeningExercises.feedback: A coffee machine is equipment; the sentence explicitly says no coffee was included.

listeningExercises.audioText: At reception, the clerk directed us to the luggage storage room rather than the meeting room.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where should the travellers take their bags?
listeningExercises.feedback: The luggage storage room is the room intended for holding bags.

listeningExercises.audioText: They booked a six-hour workshop for the new employees.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word modifier and head noun immediately after “a”.
acceptedAnswers: six-hour workshop
listeningExercises.feedback: Six-hour remains singular before the noun workshop.

listeningExercises.audioText: The tea cup was empty, but the cup of peppermint tea beside it was still warm.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which cup actually contained a drink?
listeningExercises.feedback: A cup of peppermint tea describes a drink inside; tea cup only describes an item type.

listeningExercises.audioText: Before the interview, Anika reviewed the staff training programme, not the customer satisfaction survey.
listeningExercises.feedback: The staff training programme, rather than the survey, was reviewed.

listeningExercises.audioText: The updated factory safety inspection report is finished, but the actual inspection starts on Friday.
listeningExercises.feedback: The report is finished; the inspection itself is scheduled for Friday.

listeningExercises.audioText: There is a passport scanner at the boarding gate for checking documents.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word noun compound immediately after “a”.
acceptedAnswers: passport scanner
listeningExercises.feedback: Passport modifies the head noun scanner; passport stays singular.

listeningExercises.audioText: Visitors can collect their visitor parking permit at the main reception desk.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word noun compound between “their” and “at”.
acceptedAnswers: visitor parking permit
listeningExercises.feedback: Visitor parking permit is a compound headed by permit.
